title_en: The rabbit decided, the rabbit dandy
background: It is the rabbit's wedding day. A dandy rabbit dresses up and gets engaged to a widowed fox. He invites an animal wedding party: a she-bear, a she-wolf as godmother, a frog on the *zurla* (folk oboe) and a hedgehog on the drum. He crosses the plain of Solun (Thessaloniki) to fetch his bride, finds a mother hen with chicks instead, runs into hunters and bolts, shouting that he is no bridegroom. It is a parody of a village wedding, and kids love it. *Kokorajko* is a playful rhyming nickname with no exact meaning, roughly "cocky little bunny". The song is packed with Turkish loanwords ending in *-džija* (one who does a job), a trace of Ottoman-era speech. Pesna.org lists two versions, and this page shows both. A couple of dialect words (*lindra lija*, *džimrika*) have no clean English equivalent.

lines.cyr: Сторил ниет зајко, зајко да се жени,
lines.lat: Storil niet zajko, zajko da se ženi,
lines.en: The rabbit made up his mind, the rabbit would marry,
rabbit dandy, the daring rabbit,
he shook out his trousers, twirled up his moustache,
put on his vest and a sporty cap,

lines.cyr: Море, што мислете бре? Личи на младоженја!
lines.lat: More, što mislete bre? Liči na mladoženja!
lines.en: Hey, what do you think? He looks like a bridegroom!
The rabbit got engaged to a fox, a widow,
sorrowful and worn down, a rooster for a neighbor,
a well-known fusspot, pampered and spoiled,
a worldly hermit,
hey, the village chatterbox!
The rabbit invited his prettily dressed wedding guests:
a she-bear butcher, a she-wolf godmother,
a hedgehog drummer, a frog zurna player,
a shaggy herald,
the rabbit dandy,
he shook out his trousers, twirled up his moustache,
put on his vest and a sporty cap,
hey, a perfect bridegroom!
